open_errors.issue: At dawn at the east-track junction Kunal says Ranu is 'a day down the Garh road', yet they reach Ranu at noon the same day. That noon arrival is when he sends the runner his dawn plan said would reach Sarn fold 'by dusk today'.
open_errors.fix: Make Ranu half a day down the Garh road from the junction.

patches.find: "Ranu is a day down the Garh road. Part of the way I mean to show you starts there.
patches.replace: "Ranu is half a day down the Garh road. Part of the way I mean to show you starts there.

open_errors.issue: Ila says Kunal's paces are longer than hers by two fingers. She then converts three hundred of his paces into only two hundred and seventy of hers, which would need her pace to be the longer one.
open_errors.fix: Make the conversion run the right way: three hundred of his paces is about three hundred and thirty of hers.

patches.find: Let the stone be somewhere in this hump. Two hundred and seventy of mine.
patches.replace: Let the stone be somewhere in this hump. Three hundred and thirty of mine.

open_errors.issue: Chapter 17 fixes the bond at day ten, with ten strokes in the petition margin and ten days of watching her field book. Chapter 20 happens that same night, but both leads say 'twelve days'.

patches.find: In twelve days he had learned this about her: she waited like a woman holding a level, to see which way the bubble went.
patches.replace: In ten days he had learned this about her: she waited like a woman holding a level, to see which way the bubble went.

patches.find: "I've watched you for twelve days," said Ila.
patches.replace: "I've watched you for ten days," said Ila.

open_errors.issue: In chapter 24 Ila draws the nail and takes the hide note down after Kunal lifts the whistle off. Chapter 27 says he took the whistle 'with the note still pinned beside it'.
open_errors.fix: Say he lifted the whistle from above the note, without claiming the note stayed pinned.

patches.find: He had lifted it off the lintel nail at the hut, with the note still pinned beside it, and he had not taken it off since.
patches.replace: He had lifted it off the lintel nail at the hut, from above the note, and he had not taken it off since.

open_errors.issue: The pair leave the Under-Cairn and come out at the Shilak Cairn at dawn, then spend that day and night in the salt house. Meera's knock the next morning is day sixteen. Day seventeen is therefore not 'the morning after the Under-Cairn'.
open_errors.fix: Anchor day seventeen to Meera's knock.

patches.find: On the seventeenth day of the rope, the morning after the Under-Cairn, Ila pinned two sheets
patches.replace: On the seventeenth day of the rope, the morning after Meera's knock, Ila pinned two sheets

open_errors.issue: Under the Winter Crossing Law the rope is eight spans of the guide's own arm. In chapter 3 Ila measures the rope against her own arm 'because she was the guide'. But chapter 2 puts Kunal's name on her licence's guide line, and chapter 1 has the licence ask the council to 'name a guide'. That would make the rope his arm's length.
open_errors.fix: Have the licence ask the council for a bound partner, not a guide, so Ila stays the guide whose arm sets the rope.

patches.find: I have a licence application, four lines, asking the council to name a guide and bind me to him at the cairn.
patches.replace: I have a licence application, four lines, asking the council to name a partner and bind me to him at the cairn.

patches.find: With it, the council would name a guide for her, bind her to him at the cairn, and she could cross the Saddle.
patches.replace: With it, the council would name a partner for her, bind her to him at the cairn, and she could cross the Saddle.

patches.find: On the line left for the guide's name, the pencil had already been there.
patches.replace: On the line left for the partner's name, the pencil had already been there.
